Structure_Text.original: In the as-cast sample, the grains formed during the solidification are equiaxial with a diameter between 10 and 20 μm. Irregular-shaped Nb-rich Laves_C14 phase forms along grain boundaries as the predominant precipitate. A small fraction of blocky NbC carbides is encompassed by the Laves_C14 precipitates.

Structure_Text.original: After 12-h homogenization, the Laves_C14 phase dissolves completely, and only NbC carbides can be observed as precipitates. Significantly coarsened grains can be found in sample AC12h with some small grains remained at the triple junctions of these coarsened grains. A trimodal grain size distribution can be observed, with two peaks appearing with smaller grain diameters of 150 μm and 400 μm. Abnormal grain growth during homogenization.
Structure_Text.simplified: Laves_C14 fully dissolved, only NbC remains, abnormal grain growth with coarsened grains, trimodal distribution

Structure_Text.original: Due to the large directional thermal gradient introduced by laser melting, columnar grains grow along the direction normal to the edge of single arc-shaped melt pools. Both very fine columnar (with a width of ~1 μm) and cellular (with a diameter of ~2 μm) subgrains can be found within the relatively larger grains of the overlapped melt pool areas. The only secondary phase observed in the as-built sample is the Laves_C14 phase, which forms along grain boundaries of both the columnar and cellular subgrains due to Nb segregation.
Structure_Text.simplified: Columnar grains with fine columnar (~1 μm wide) and cellular (~2 μm diameter) subgrains, Laves_C14 along subgrain boundaries, no NbC observed

Texture_or_Orientation.Note: Columnar grains grow along direction normal to edge of arc-shaped melt pools in X-Z plane (building direction Z); anisotropic grain texture

Structure_Text.original: The grain size in sample AM12h after 12-h isothermal treatment at 1180 °C is even smaller than AM20m. The grain size distribution of AM12h is close to unimodal. Dispersed NbC particles distribute along and near grain boundaries, confirming Zener pinning effect. A large number of dislocations were found in the vicinity of NbC carbides and grain boundaries. NbC carbides around 200~300 nm in diameter are dislocation sources. Small NbC carbides have coherency with γ matrix. The dislocation-precipitate interaction follows both Orowan bowing and dislocation cutting mechanisms. Dislocation arrays/loops are planar; tanglings and cells seldom found.
Structure_Text.simplified: Unimodal grain size distribution (refined), NbC Zener pinning, dislocation arrays/loops near NbC, Orowan + cutting mechanisms, planar dislocations

Secondary_Phases.Morphology: dispersed along and near grain boundaries

Size.Note: larger NbC carbides that act as dislocation sources

Coherency.Large_NbC: loss of coherency with γ matrix
Coherency.Note: Orientation_Relationship uses overline notation for negative Miller indices; OCR text used negative sign as substitute

Grain_Size.Note: Average grain size; smaller than AM20m, refined by recrystallization

GOS.Note: Slightly increased compared with AM1h but still at low level; attributed to deformation induced by Nb accumulation to form more NbC carbides

Stacking_Fault_Energy_Range.Note: intermediate SFE of Inconel 718, from Sundararaman et al. [91,92]; inhibits cross slip during homogenization, prevents stacking fault formation

Advanced_Quantitative_Features.Dislocation_Behavior_Note: Small particles: dislocations cut through; Large particles: dislocations bow around. Dislocation arrays pile up at grain boundaries.

Composition.Note: CALPHAD calculation using nominal Inconel 718 composition

Structure_Text.original: The NbC carbide is stable at high temperatures, even at 1200 °C, and thus often co-exists with the γ matrix phase during homogenization. The δ phase is stable up to 1034 °C. The γ" phase is metastable and will transform into the δ phase after long-time aging. The formation temperature of NbC carbides (1298 °C) is higher than that of the Laves_C14 phase (1170 °C).
Structure_Text.simplified: CALPHAD predictions: NbC stable at >1200°C, δ stable up to 1034°C, γ" metastable, NbC formation at 1298°C, Laves_C14 at 1170°C
